postimage.digest_sources_note: Two of the four are now ISSUED documents: the acceptances were issued by an independent party at dd6ed30 (round 2, after round 1 refused the subject on NW02-R1), and the sources point at the issued files rather than the skeletons. The subject is final at e75176b5. The FOURTH, the signature evidence, is still the skeleton and still carries its sentinels, because it captures the continuation merge that publishes the subject and the two acceptances -- a merge that has not happened. It keeps pointing at the skeleton deliberately: the generator's S12 is what stops a skeleton digest reaching the database, and giving the field a non-hex placeholder instead breaks S7 and disables that very check. So this instance still may not execute. What changed is why: one missing merge, not three missing documents.

in_transaction_window_assertion.what: clock_timestamp() >= not_before and < expires_at, asserted inside the transaction in BOTH the pre-block and the post-block
in_transaction_window_assertion.why: NW-01 had this only in the read-only preflight, outside the transaction. It is the one guard of the sixteen that flips with time, so a delay between preflight and apply could commit an already-expired window. NW01ExecutionReceipt.preflight.why_that_mattered records that only operational discipline stood in for it.

sole_non_internal_trigger_assertion.what: exactly one non-internal trigger on clued_control.accepted_binding, named accepted_binding_immutable, asserted in BOTH blocks
sole_non_internal_trigger_assertion.why: NW-01 asserted the definition and tgenabled of the trigger it names, but nothing stopped a SECOND non-internal trigger from existing. NW01ExecutionReceipt.read_back.non_internal_trigger_note measured it after the fact and said the assertion still belongs in the transaction.
